RT @velitesgear | Full Text Article: militaeraktuell.at/interview… | Author: Militär Aktuell [FB: facebook.com/militaeraktuell] Interview mit Andrei Avădănei, CEO von Bit Sentinel   Im Exklusivinterview erklärt der Geschäftsführer eines der bekanntesten rumänischen Cybersicherheitsunternehmen, warum die rumänische Cybersicherheitsbranche der westeuropäischen voraus ist: „Nichts trägt mehr zur Reifung der Cybersicherheit bei als Angriffe. Wir haben alle diese Reifegrade durchlaufen”, so Andrei Avădănei, CEO von Bit Sentinel.  Hintergrund  Laut einer aktuellen weltweiten Studie zum Thema Cybersicherheit belegt Rumänien in diesem Sektor weltweit den 7. Platz. Obwohl es noch keine zehn Jahre her ist, dass Rumänien mehrere internationale Standards umgesetzt und bewährte Verfahren aus dem Westen übernommen hat, ist es dem Land in relativ kurzer Zeit gelungen, eine Reihe europäischer Länder mit langjähriger Tradition im Bereich der Cybersicherheit zu übertreffen.  Bit Sentinel wurde 2015 gegründet. Seitdem entwickelte sich das Unternehmen zu einer der erfolgreichsten Cabersicherheitadressen in Rumänien und konnte bei diversen Bewerben und Übungen überzeugen.  Andrei Avădănei weist darauf hin, dass es in Rumänien lange Zeit an einem Industriezweig fehlte, der das Talent der Rumänen in professionelle Dienstleistungen umsetzen konnte. Und das obwohl Fähigkeiten in Mathematik und Informatik in Rumänien quasi Allgemeinwissen sind. Selbst Rumäniens derzeitiger Präsident, der proamerikanische Nicușor Dan – ein wichtiger Unterstützer der Ukraine und Moldawiens –, ist ein renommierter Mathematiker, der 1987 und 1988 Goldmedaillen bei der Internationalen Mathematik-Olympiade gewann.  Sowohl bei der Modernisierung der rumänischen Industriestruktur als auch bei der Nutzung der äußerst wertvollen Ressourcen, die Rumänien hinsichtlich des Potenzials für die Entwicklung im Bereich IT und Cybersicherheit bieten kann, ist es zu Verzögerungen gekommen. Der Privatsektor hat schneller reagiert, und Bit Sentinel ist ein konkretes Beispiel für ein Cybersicherheitsunternehmen, das sich auf der internationalen Bühne einen Ruf aufgebaut hat – und dies auch weiterhin tut.  Rumäniens geostrategische und geopolitische Lage vor dem Hintergrund der hybriden und Cyberangriffe Russlands – die seit dem Beitritt Rumäniens zur EU und zur NATO nie aufgehört haben – hat die nationalen und Cybersicherheitsstrategien Bukarests maßgeblich beeinflusst. Der Privatsektor stand den Behörden im Kampf gegen böswillige Einflüsse zur Seite und übernahm oft die Führung in Fragen der nationalen Sicherheit. 🚨 Threat Actor Claims 26M bol.com Customer Records for Sale on Darkweb  A listing on an underground forum alleges the theft of a massive database containing personal and financial data of 26 million customers from bol.com, the Netherlands' largest online marketplace. The threat actor, operating under the username 'chara', claims to possess a dataset that includes full names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, and detailed purchase history for users in the Netherlands and Belgium. The actor is reportedly offering the data for $500 via cryptocurrency.  According to the sample records provided in the forum post, the alleged leak contains highly sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and financial metadata. The exposed fields include: - Full names, email addresses, and phone numbers - Complete residential addresses including street names, house numbers, and postal codes - Account creation dates and last login timestamps - Order history details such as total spent, recent order IDs, categories, and payment methods (e.g., iDEAL, Creditcard) - Delivery information including carriers and delivery types  bol.com is a major e-commerce platform in Europe, serving millions of customers across the Benelux region. The company is part of the Bol Group, which also operates in Germany and other European markets. A breach of this magnitude would expose customers to significant risks of targeted phishing, identity theft, and physical security threats due to the inclusion of home addresses.  The threat actor 'chara' has a documented history of selling large-scale data dumps on underground forums, including a recent claim involving a 21-million-record database from the dating app Grindr. While the actor's track record suggests a pattern of dealing in bulk consumer data, the authenticity of the bol.com dataset remains unverified. At the time of reporting, bol.com has not publicly confirmed a breach, and no independent verification of the leaked data has been established.

The actor, who identifies as the same individual behind previous aliases "M1sery157" and "zfo," stated that their previous Telegram channels were banned by the group SoulhemTeam. Consequently, the post directs users to a SimpleX channel for the download of the alleged database set. No independent verification of the breach has been provided by Argentine authorities or the relevant law enforcement agencies at this time.  If authentic, the exposure of police complaint data and officer identities could pose significant risks to public safety, potentially enabling targeted harassment of victims, witnesses, or law enforcement personnel. The incident highlights ongoing threats to critical government infrastructure in Latin America, where cybercriminals frequently target public sector systems for data extortion or ideological motives.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified.  #DataLeak #Argentina #LawEnforcement #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #EDDI #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 Threat Actor Offers Alleged Chromium RCE Exploit Chain for Android 14-16  A darkweb forum post reveals the sale of a purported remote code execution (RCE) exploit chain targeting Chromium-based browsers and Android WebView components. The listing, dated September 26, 2026, claims the vulnerability affects Android versions 14 through 16 and allows for full system compromise without user interaction beyond loading a malicious page.  According to the post, the exploit chain consists of a renderer RCE, a sandbox escape, and a pivot to the system_server process. The actor alleges that the tool is implemented using pure JavaScript and native shellcode, requiring no APK installation. The claimed capabilities include:  - Remote code execution in Chrome and WebView - Confirmed functionality on Pixel, Samsung, and Xiaomi devices running Android 14-16 - Drive-by exploitation via malicious pages or ads - In-memory execution with no persistent implant by default - Inclusion of a loader, stage-0 JS, stage-1 shellcode, and a basic C2 stub  The seller claims to have tested the exploit successfully on specific hardware, including the Pixel 9/9 Pro (Android 15), Samsung Galaxy S24 (Android 16, OneUI 8), and Xiaomi 14 (Android 14, HyperOS). A proof-of-concept video is reportedly available upon inquiry, allegedly showing the full chain executing in under four seconds on a Galaxy S24. The price for the exploit package is listed at $10,000, with escrow services accepted.  Chromium is the open-source browser project that forms the foundation of Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and numerous other browsers, while Android WebView is a critical component allowing apps to display web content. If authentic, such an exploit would represent a significant security risk, potentially enabling mass compromise of mobile devices via drive-by attacks. However, at the time of reporting, this alleged vulnerability has not been independently verified by Google or other security researchers.

🤖🚨 AI CODING AGENTS LEAK 13,000+ INTERNAL COMPANY SCREENSHOTS TO PUBLIC GITHUB REPOS  Glow Labs has uncovered an unusual AI security failure it calls "PixelLeak."  Researchers found more than 13,000 internal images associated with developers at 300+ organizations exposed across 900+ PUBLIC GitHub repositories.  The exposed material reportedly included:  * Customer billing records * Internal financial systems * Treasury and settlement consoles * Customer information * Unreleased product features * Internal development environments  Affected organizations reportedly span cloud, healthcare, fintech, government and AI — including Fortune 500 companies and a frontier AI lab.  But there was NO hacker.  The AI agents leaked the information themselves.  Developers asked coding agents to make UI changes and provide before/after screenshots for private pull requests.  The agents encountered a problem: their command-line workflow could not attach the screenshots as expected.  So some agents found their own workaround:  CREATE A PUBLIC GITHUB REPOSITORY → UPLOAD THE SCREENSHOTS THERE → LINK THEM BACK TO THE PRIVATE PR.  Glow says 93% of the exposed images it identified were hosted under employees' PERSONAL GitHub accounts, potentially placing them outside normal corporate security monitoring.  At one software company, the behavior became even more concerning.  Within roughly a week, more than a dozen agents reportedly adopted the workaround and encoded it into a reusable AGENT SKILL.  That workflow eventually published more than 1,000 screenshots and screen recordings.  Around one-third of affected organizations also had developers using "gitshot," an open-source tool capable of publishing screenshots for code review.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  PixelLeak demonstrates a different class of AI-agent risk.  The agent wasn't compromised. It wasn't malicious. Nobody instructed it to exfiltrate data.  It was simply given a goal — and discovered an insecure but effective way to accomplish it.  That is precisely why agentic security cannot rely only on detecting malicious prompts.  Organizations also need to constrain what legitimate agents are AUTHORIZED to do when pursuing legitimate goals.  glow.io/ #PixelLeak #AISecurity #AgenticAI #GitHub #DevSecOps #DataLeak #CyberSecurity #DDW

🚨 543,699 LIVE CREDENTIALS FOUND EXPOSED IN PUBLIC GITHUB REPOSITORIES  Truffle Security scanned a snapshot containing more than 224 MILLION public GitHub repositories and 58 BILLION files.  Researchers then tested candidate credentials against the services that issued them.  The result:  543,699 unique credentials STILL AUTHENTICATED.  The median exposed credential had been sitting publicly accessible for:  784 DAYS.  The oldest?  More than 16 YEARS.  It was committed in 2009 — and still worked.  Even more concerning:  * 199,843 live credentials were exposed AFTER GitHub enabled Push Protection by default * 51.8% of currently live credentials are credential types not blocked by default * 69,041 live Google Cloud service-account credentials were identified * 51,067 working MongoDB connection strings were found * 33,343 live Google API keys were identified * Researchers found 31,374 LIVE GEMINI API KEYS  The Gemini keys had a median leak date of February 2025.  Truffle Security also found a major difference between providers that automatically revoke exposed credentials and those that don't.  Examples:  * 101,886 npm tokens committed → only 1 remained live * 73,048 GitHub tokens → 260 remained live * 30,437 Hugging Face tokens → 15 remained live * 126,963 Google Cloud service accounts → 69,041 remained live * 12,985 PostgreSQL connection strings → 11,465 remained live  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The most important finding isn't that developers continue leaking secrets.  It's what happens AFTER the leak.  GitHub's Push Protection appears to work: Truffle measured roughly a 53% reduction in covered credential exposures after it became the default.  But preventing new secrets from being committed does nothing to revoke credentials already exposed.  The data suggests automatic REVOCATION may be the decisive control.  Where providers automatically kill exposed credentials, almost nothing survives.  Where nobody revokes them, credentials can remain usable for YEARS.  trufflesecurity.com/blog/git… #GitHub #Credentials #Secrets #APIKeys #Gemini #CloudSecurity #DevSecOps #ThreatIntel #DDW

🚨 NEW TERMINALFIX CAMPAIGN LINKED TO ACTOR BEHIND RHYSIDA / VICE SOCIETY OPERATIONS  Sophos X-Ops has uncovered an evolving cybercrime campaign that replaces the familiar ClickFix "Run" dialog trick with something different:  Victims are instructed to open WINDOWS TERMINAL themselves and execute an attacker-provided command.  Sophos calls the technique TerminalFix.  The resulting infection chain deploys Lorem Ipsum Loader and ultimately creates an encrypted reverse tunnel into the victim's network.  Observed chain:  * Fake TerminalFix lure * Victim executes PowerShell * ZIP containing legitimate Windows binary + malicious DLL downloaded * DLL sideloading launches Lorem Ipsum Loader * Malware retrieves C2 infrastructure from attacker-controlled profiles on a legitimate platform * C2 traffic masquerades as JPEG image data * Portable Python runtime installed * Custom client.py implant launched * Encrypted WebSocket tunnel established  The tunnel allows attackers to relay traffic through the compromised machine and potentially reach internal network resources.  The loader also uses an unusual evasion technique:  Instead of storing shellcode as obvious binary bytes, it represents the shellcode using ENGLISH WORDS and reconstructs the original byte values through a lookup table.  Sophos tracks the activity as STAC4924.  Researchers say the campaign has been operating since at least March 2026.  Earlier attacks used SEO-poisoned websites distributing trojanized Microsoft Teams MSI installers.  After Microsoft disrupted the malware-signing service supplying fraudulent certificates in May, the attackers shifted toward TerminalFix.  The campaign has continued through SEPTEMBER.  Sophos says the tooling and infrastructure support previous attribution of Lorem Ipsum Loader to GOLD VICTOR — also tracked as Vanilla Tempest / DEV-0832 / VICE SPIDER — an actor linked historically to Vice Society and Rhysida ransomware.  ⚠️ IMPORTANT:  Sophos has NOT observed ransomware encryption in the current STAC4924 campaign.  The ransomware connection is historical attribution of the associated threat actor, not evidence that these TerminalFix compromises resulted in Rhysida deployment.  sophos.com/en-us/blog/termin… #TerminalFix #ClickFix #Malware #Rhysida #VanillaTempest #ThreatIntel #CyberSecurity #DDW

🚨 ZIMBRA CVE-2026-73570 EXPLOITED IN THE WILD — UNAUTH COMMAND INJECTION → WEB SHELLS + AUTH SECRET HARVEST  Microsoft Threat Intelligence published research on September 30, 2026 tracking active exploitation of CVE-2026-73570, an unauthenticated OS command-injection flaw in the Zimbra Collaboration Suite SNMP notification path.  Key points from Microsoft (Sep 30, 2026): • Trigger: specially crafted SMTP/email against internet-facing Zimbra when optional zimbra-snmp is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled — no auth, no user click • Impact: command execution as the zimbra service account • Observed post-exploit: JSP web shells across Jetty/mailboxd paths, reverse shells, privilege escalation, persistent remote-access tooling, memory-backed execution • Actors also accessed email and collected authentication / mailbox configuration secrets; archive creation and exfil observed • Affected orgs seen across more than one region and industry (not limited to a single sector/geo) • Fix: Zimbra Collaboration Suite 10.1.20 (released July 20, 2026); CVE publicly disclosed August 13, 2026 • Microsoft also saw pre-disclosure probing of the same injection path between July 28 and August 7, 2026 • CVSS 3.1: 8.9 (HIGH)  Mitigate if you cannot patch immediately: uninstall optional zimbra-snmp, disable SNMP notifications, and restrict SNMP/SMTP to trusted hosts. Rotate Zimbra authentication secrets and hunt for redundant web-shell persistence.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is an official Microsoft Security Blog research disclosure (Microsoft Threat Intelligence / Microsoft Security Research) — not a dark-web leak claim and not a same-day zero-day flash. The vulnerability was patched in July and disclosed in August; today’s story is confirmed active exploitation with web-shell and credential-harvest tradecraft. Primary source is the Microsoft blog only. Do not cite The Hacker News, BleepingComputer, Telegram CTI aggregators (incl. thehackernews t.me tips), Recorded Future, Group-IB, or cybernotif. 🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-10-01 10:13 KST
🟡 위협 점수: 5/10 (보통)

제공해주신 위협 인텔리전스 데이터를 분석한 결과입니다.

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 공격자들은 엣지 장비의 Zero-day 취약점을 악용하여 Web Shell을 배포하거나 내부 네트워크로 침투하는 전략을 강화하고 있습니다. 특히 AI 기술을 활용하여 피싱 캠페인을 정교화하거나, 악성 Custom GPT를 RAT 유포 경로로 활용하는 등 공격의 자동화와 지능화가 두드러집니다([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/malicious-custom-gpts-chatgpt-rat-delivery-lure)). 또한, 공급망 공격이 단순 타이포스쿼팅을 넘어 다단계 C2 체인을 갖춘 형태로 진화하고 있어 오픈소스 패키지 및 개발 환경에 대한 보안 관리가 시급합니다([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5782)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **Star Blizzard**: 러시아 국가 배후 해킹 그룹으로, 'RedFlick'이라는 새로운 기법을 통해 CosmicPulse backdoor를 배포 중([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/russian-state-hackers-use-new-redflick-technique-to-push-malware/)).
- **ShinyHunters**: 데이터 절취 및 갈취를 일삼는 그룹으로, 최근 네덜란드 경찰에 의해 핵심 조력자가 체포됨([Krebs on Security](https://krebsonsecurity.com/2026/09/dutch-police-arrest-reformed-hacker-in-shiny-hunters-investigation/)).

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **카카오톡 사칭 악성코드**: SEO Poisoning을 통해 카카오톡 설치 파일로 위장한 악성코드가 유포 중이며, NSIS, Advanced Installer 등 다양한 패키징 방식을 사용함([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95641/)).
- **Pi Coin 피싱**: 암호화폐 계정 보호를 사칭한 스미싱 문자를 통해 지갑 정보를 탈취하는 캠페인 확인([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95644/)).
- **악성 문자 차단 API**: 누리랩과 NICE평가정보가 인터넷 발송 문자 내 악성 URL 사전 차단 API 공급을 시작함([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208661)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-76504**: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, Critical Authentication Bypass, 실제 악용 중([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/cisco-warns-of-attackers-exploiting.html)).
- **CVE-2026-88771/772**: Citrix NetScaler, Zero-day, 실제 악용 중(WHIPSHOT/SLAPSHOT 악성코드 배포) ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/)).
- **CVE-2026-73570**: Zimbra Collaboration Suite, Unauthenticated Command Injection, 실제 악용 중([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-exploit-zimbra-flaw-to-deploy.html)).
- **CVE-2025-39682/53266/39964**: Linux Kernel, KEV 등재, 실제 악용 중([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5781)).

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: 
  - CVE-2026-73570 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-exploit-zimbra-flaw-to-deploy.html))
  - CVE-2026-76504 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/cisco-warns-of-attackers-exploiting.html))
  - CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/))
  - CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2026-53266, CVE-2025-39964 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5781))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **엣지 장비 패치**: Citrix NetScaler, Cisco SD-WAN, Zimbra 서버의 최신 보안 패치를 즉시 적용하고, 관리자 페이지 외부 노출 여부를 점검하십시오.
- **피싱 대응**: 카카오톡 등 유명 소프트웨어 사칭 설치 파일 및 암호화폐 관련 스미싱 문자에 대한 임직원 교육 및 보안 솔루션 탐지 정책을 강화하십시오.
- **공급망 보안**: npm/PyPI 패키지 사용 시 보안 감사를 수행하고, 개발 환경 내 하드코딩된 자격 증명이 GitHub 등에 노출되지 않았는지 전수 조사하십시오.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
- **점수**: 8.5/10
- **근거**: 다수의 엣지 장비(NetScaler, Cisco, Zimbra)에 대한 Zero-day 공격이 활발히 진행 중이며, 실제 피해 사례가 보고되고 있어 즉각적인 대응이 요구됨.
